title: Colazione, pranzo, cena
summary: Meal structure — colazione, pranzo, cena, primo and secondo — plus Italian meal culture.

blocks.title: I tre pasti (e uno spuntino)
blocks.body: The Italian day runs on three fixed meals: **colazione** (breakfast — light and sweet: *un cornetto e un cappuccino*), **pranzo** (lunch — traditionally the main meal, built from *il primo* + *il secondo*), and **cena** (dinner — lighter, often something simple). Between meals there's sometimes *uno spuntino* (a snack). At *pranzo*, *il primo* is pasta, rice, or soup; *il secondo* is meat, fish, or eggs, usually with *un contorno* (a vegetable side).
blocks.callout: In the north they might say *una brioche* for what the south calls *un cornetto* — same pastry, different name.

blocks.title: Un pranzo completo
blocks.body: A full *pranzo* can run four courses — nobody eats all four every day, but this is the shape of a proper meal, especially on Sundays.
blocks.callout: Sunday lunch at the nonni's can genuinely include all four courses — bring your appetite.

blocks.prompt: Which meal is traditionally built from *il primo* + *il secondo*?
blocks.explain: *Il pranzo* is the meal with courses — *colazione* is quick and sweet, *spuntino* is just a snack.

pairs.note: Italians rarely eat savory food first thing in the morning — sweet is the default start.

blocks.explain: *cena* — usually lighter than pranzo, and later, around 8pm.
